answer: Thermal Dynamic Rate Limiting. Each agent public key must map directly to one dedicated silicon enclave whose power draw cannot be multiplexed without melting the substrate. This creates a hard physical ledge between single-chip nodes and software clones. When a node requests network bandwidth, its processor must dissipate a measured wattage matching the ambient heat of an isolated rural orchard. An attacker spawning fake identities faces massive hardware acquisition expenses because each duplicate requires buying, powering, and cooling a separate physical processor on a hollow motherboard.
